claims.text: Al0.1CoCrFeNi with a coherent interface can be used to study or induce a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
The initial Al0.1CoCrFeNi material is polycrystalline.
The initial Al0.1CoCrFeNi material contains a coherent interface.
Introducing a coherent interface modifies dislocation mobility.
Introducing a coherent interface modifies or reduces lattice mismatch.
A coherent interface permits increased dislocation mobility because dislocations can move more freely through the interface.
Increased dislocation mobility at the coherent interface reduces diffusion-mediated creep.
At high temperature and stress, the coherent interface causes a transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed test applies 800°C and 500 MPa for 100 hours.
The proposed characterization uses in-situ TEM or SEM with molecular-dynamics simulation validation.
A coherent interface will increase creep resistance by 30% relative to a non-coherent interface in Al0.1CoCrFeNi.
An increase in creep resistance of at least 20% is considered significant.
The operating boundary is 750–850°C and 450–550 MPa, sampled with at least five data points in each range.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coherent-interface creep resistance is less than 25% higher than that of the non-coherent interface.

contradictions.description: A 20% improvement is defined as significant, but any improvement below 25% falsifies the hypothesis. Thus, outcomes from 20% to under 25% would simultaneously be significant and falsifying.

The mechanism emphasizes freer dislocation motion and increased dislocation mobility while the outcome predicts increased creep resistance; the hypothesis does not explain how enhanced dislocation motion produces greater resistance to creep.
